terms.definition: A service for centrally managing and governing multiple AWS accounts from a single management account
terms.example: Like a university admin office managing multiple departments, each with its own AWS account

terms.definition: The primary AWS account that creates and controls an AWS Organization (also called master account)
terms.example: Your main company AWS account that invites or creates all subsidiary team accounts

terms.definition: An AWS account that belongs to an AWS Organization and is governed by the management account via SCPs
terms.example: A development team's AWS account added to the organization by the master account

terms.definition: A logical grouping of AWS accounts within Organizations, similar to a folder — policies attached to an OU apply to all accounts inside it
terms.example: Dev-OU contains all development team accounts; attaching an SCP to Dev-OU affects all those accounts

terms.definition: A JSON policy document in AWS Organizations that sets maximum permissions for all users and roles (including root) in a member account
terms.example: An SCP denying ec2:* means nobody in that account — not even root — can use EC2

terms.definition: A feature of AWS Organizations that combines the charges of all member accounts into a single invoice paid by the management account
terms.example: Like a family mobile plan — all lines use services independently but one person pays the combined monthly bill

terms.definition: Web Application Firewall — filters HTTP/HTTPS web requests to protect applications from attacks like SQL injection, XSS, and bots at Layer 7
terms.example: Blocks 10,000 fake bot requests per second while letting through real user requests to your registration website

terms.definition: Web Access Control List — the WAF construct that contains all your WAF rules and is attached to a protected resource like CloudFront or ALB
terms.example: A Web ACL named 'prod-security' containing geo-block rules, rate-limit rules, and managed rule groups

terms.definition: A WAF rule that blocks or counts requests from a single IP that exceed a defined threshold in a time window
terms.example: Block any IP sending more than 1,000 requests in 5 minutes — automatically stops bot floods

terms.definition: Distributed Denial of Service — an attack using many compromised computers to flood a target with traffic, making it unavailable to legitimate users
terms.example: Hackers controlling 10,000 infected computers all sending fake requests to your website simultaneously, crashing your server

terms.definition: Free, automatic DDoS protection for all AWS customers at the network and transport layers (L3/L4)
terms.example: Automatically protects your CloudFront distributions and Route 53 hosted zones from SYN floods without any configuration

terms.definition: Paid enhanced DDoS protection (~$3,000/month) that adds L7 protection, 24/7 DRT access, and cost reimbursement for scaling during attacks
terms.example: An e-commerce company uses Shield Advanced to ensure uptime during Black Friday when DDoS attacks are more likely

terms.definition: Automated vulnerability scanning service that continuously assesses EC2 instances, ECR container images, and Lambda functions for known CVEs and network exposure
terms.example: Inspector scans your EC2 fleet overnight and reports: 'Instance i-123 has CVE-2023-4511 in package openssl 1.0.2 — update immediately'

terms.definition: Common Vulnerability and Exposure — a standardized identifier for a publicly known cybersecurity vulnerability in software
terms.example: CVE-2021-44228 is the Log4Shell vulnerability — Inspector would detect if your instance uses a vulnerable Log4j version

terms.definition: A service that records configuration changes to AWS resources over time and evaluates those against compliance rules
terms.example: Config detects that a developer changed a security group to allow SSH from 0.0.0.0/0 at 3:47 PM and flags it as NON_COMPLIANT

terms.definition: The status AWS Config assigns to a resource when its configuration violates a Config rule
terms.example: S3 bucket 'employee-data' marked NON_COMPLIANT because it allows public read access — violating the s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited rule

terms.definition: A threat detection service that continuously monitors AWS accounts for malicious activity using machine learning on CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs
terms.example: GuardDuty detects at 3 AM that a compromised IAM key is making API calls from Russia — fires a finding for investigation

terms.definition: An alert generated by GuardDuty when it detects suspicious or malicious activity, categorized by type and severity
terms.example: Finding: 'UnauthorizedAccess:EC2/SSHBruteForce' means someone is repeatedly trying SSH passwords on your EC2 instance

terms.definition: A centralized security dashboard that aggregates findings from multiple AWS security services (GuardDuty, Inspector, Config, Macie) and third-party tools into one view
terms.example: Security Hub shows 47 active findings: 3 critical from GuardDuty, 12 high from Inspector, 32 medium from Config

terms.definition: A service that analyzes resource-based policies to identify resources accessible from outside your AWS account or organization
terms.example: Access Analyzer finds that an S3 bucket has a bucket policy granting GetObject to '*' (everyone) — flags it as a public access finding

terms.definition: In IAM Access Analyzer, the boundary (account or organization) within which access is considered expected — access from outside triggers a finding
terms.example: Setting zone of trust to your AWS Organization means Access Analyzer flags any role assumable by accounts outside your organization

terms.definition: A data security service using machine learning to automatically discover, classify, and protect sensitive data (PII, financial, credentials) in Amazon S3
terms.example: Macie scans 500,000 files in your data lake S3 bucket overnight and reports: '47 objects contain credit card numbers; 3 of those buckets are publicly accessible'

terms.definition: Personally Identifiable Information — data that can identify a specific individual, such as name, SSN, passport number, or date of birth
terms.example: An employee export file containing names, addresses, and social security numbers is PII — Macie detects and flags it

terms.definition: A security investigation service that uses machine learning on CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and GuardDuty findings to help analyze the root cause and timeline of security incidents
terms.example: After GuardDuty fires an alert, Detective shows: the compromised key first appeared at 2:31 AM, made 47 API calls, accessed 3 S3 buckets

terms.definition: A systematic examination of digital evidence to reconstruct what happened during a security incident — who, what, when, where, and how
terms.example: Amazon Detective performs forensic analysis by correlating CloudTrail API calls with VPC Flow Log connections and GuardDuty findings across a timeline
